sources.title: ISO 18968:2026 listing (NORMSERVIS)
findings: Retailer lists ISO 18968:2026, release date 27.8.2026, 50 pages.
sources.limits: Retailer, not ISO; iso.org/standard/85512.html returned 403.
sources.revisit: check iso.org status page and BSI for final scope text

sources.title: ISO 18968 Shaping the Future of Translation-Oriented Writing (ATC ISO blog, draft stage)
findings: Standard guides writing and evaluating texts meant for translation, for humans or machines; criteria include terminology, syntax, formatting, semantic clarity.
Excludes fiction, journalism, advertising.
sources.limits: Written while the standard was a draft; clause text not seen.
sources.revisit: buy or preview the final standard before citing clauses

sources.title: ISO 24495-3:2026 Plain language - Part 3: Science writing
findings: Edition 1, 2026-05, status Published.
Builds on ISO 24495-1 and is organized by its four principles.
Science writing for readers with varying education levels; not journal articles. Applies to mostly text-and-image material, most written languages.
sources.limits: Scope abstract only; part 1 not opened.
sources.revisit: open ISO 24495-1:2023 abstract when iso.org is reachable

sources.title: ISO House Style (committee.iso.org mirror)
findings: Use plain language so readers can find, understand and use information; it reduces misunderstanding.
Documents have non-native readers and are often translated; clear concise writing avoids translation errors.
Short sentences and paragraphs, one idea per sentence, avoid sentences over 20 words.
"shall", "must", "need to" are not interchangeable; subtle differences do not translate.
sources.limits: Written for standards drafting; 20-word limit is a house rule, not a general law.

sources.title: DIN 5008 - Rules for writing and layout of word and information processing
findings: Edition 2020-03 is marked CURRENT; commentary publication 2020-06.
Beuth record of the 2011 edition (https://www.dinmedia.de/de/norm/din-5008/137578108) says it was replaced by DIN 5008:2020-03.
sources.limits: No project/draft list consulted; absence of a notice is not proof of no revision.
sources.revisit: check DIN project portal for E DIN 5008 each quarter

sources.title: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website
findings: Generating many pages with gen AI without adding user value may violate the scaled content abuse spam policy.
It is critical to manually fact-check and review all AI-generated content before publishing, including title, meta description, structured data, image alt text.
Models predict likely word sequences and may produce inaccurate output.
sources.limits: Not a ranking guarantee; page shows no visible date.

sources.title: Email sender guidelines (Gmail)
findings: Since 2024-02-01 all senders to Gmail need SPF or DKIM, valid forward/reverse DNS, TLS, RFC 5322 format; spam rate below 0.3%.
Senders above 5,000 messages/day to Gmail must support one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed mail via List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click plus List-Unsubscribe.
Keep spam rate below 0.10% and never reach 0.30%.
sources.limits: Thresholds are per Gmail, counted per day to Gmail accounts; other mailbox providers differ.

sources.title: Email sender guidelines FAQ (Gmail)
findings: One-click unsubscribe is required only for marketing and promotional messages; transactional (password reset, reservation or form confirmations) is excluded.
Senders who already had an unsubscribe link had until 2024-06-01 to implement one-click.
From November 2025 Gmail ramps up enforcement; non-compliant traffic sees temporary and permanent rejections.
Unsubscribe link at top of message shows only for messages passing automated eligibility checks.
sources.limits: Promotional vs transactional is judged by recipients, not Google.

sources.title: RFC 8058 Signaling One-Click Functionality for List Email Headers
findings: Sender provides HTTPS POST endpoint from the List-Unsubscribe URI; it MUST NOT answer with an HTTPS redirect.
Message needs a valid authentication identifier (e.g. DKIM); URI should contain an opaque identifier; request must not carry cookies.
sources.limits: Protocol spec, not deliverability policy.

sources.title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
findings: Throughput: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time.
Instability: change fail rate and deployment rework rate (unplanned deployments caused by a production incident).
sources.limits: Page does not date the introduction of rework rate.

sources.title: DORA State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025
findings: AI's primary role is as an amplifier of existing organizational strengths and weaknesses.
Greatest returns come from the underlying organizational system, not the tools.
sources.limits: Landing page only; full report not read.

sources.title: DORA Report Finds AI Is an Amplifier ... But Trust Remains Low (InfoQ)
findings: AI adoption now correlates positively with delivery throughput, while delivery instability continues to rise.
Researchers tested whether speed offsets instability via fail-fast-fix-fast and found it did not.
sources.limits: Secondary summary; no verification/auditing-shift wording found.
sources.revisit: read primary report sections on review and batch size

sources.title: Writing good CL descriptions (Google eng-practices)
findings: CL description is a public record answering what changes and why.
First line is a short focused summary; body gives problem, why this approach, shortcomings, background links.
External links may become unreadable, so include enough context.
sources.limits: Google-internal CL culture; Gerrit-style review.

sources.title: Small CLs (Google eng-practices)
findings: Small CLs are reviewed more quickly and more thoroughly.
sources.limits: Practitioner guidance, no controlled study cited on the page.

sources.title: Pull requests (GitHub Docs)
findings: Pull requests let teams discuss and review changes before merging.
Conversation tab shows description, timeline, comments, reviews; separate tabs for commits, checks, files changed.
sources.limits: Product documentation.

sources.title: Conventional Commits 1.0.0
findings: Format <type>[scope]: <description> + optional body/footers.
Stated purpose: explicit commit history that is easier to build automated tools on; maps fix->PATCH, feat->MINOR, BREAKING CHANGE->MAJOR.
sources.limits: Does not say to use it only with automation.

sources.title: FaST Guide 2.1 (PDF)
findings: FAST = Fluid Scaling Technology, combining Open Space Technology and Open Allocation.
Optimised for design, discovery and delivery, not only delivery.
Work emerges in a Marketplace; Tribe Members self-select into teams.
Maps and Discovery Trees represent and make work visible.
sources.limits: Vendor-authored guide, 2021; no outcome evidence.
sources.revisit: Superseded for current terminology by FaST Guide v3.0 (SRC-WRITE-036), which uses Collective, not Tribe.

sources.title: FAST - Fluid Adaptive Scaling Technology (official site)
findings: Site expands the acronym as Fluid Adaptive Scaling Technology and describes self-organising around work, for delivery and discovery.
sources.limits: Marketing site, testimonials; conflicts with the guide's expansion.
sources.revisit: Superseded for current terminology by FaST Guide v3.0 (SRC-WRITE-036), which uses Collective, not Tribe.

sources.title: Professional Editorial Standards 2024
findings: Four editing stages from first iteration to last: structural, stylistic, copy editing, proofreading.
Part A fundamentals (2024 adds conscious language, accessibility); rewriting, indexing, localization out of scope.
sources.limits: English-language editing, Canadian body; definitions per stage not read (sub-pages not opened).

sources.title: GOV.UK A to Z style guide
findings: All GOV.UK content should be written in plain English with language the audience understands; "words to avoid" list exists.
sources.limits: UK English, government audience. The old gov.uk/guidance/style-guide URL moved; the page was opened on its current host on 2026-11-24 (title, heading and index confirmed, entries not read in full).

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide - Highlights
findings: Conversational tone, active voice, second person, writing for accessibility and a global audience, descriptive link text.
sources.limits: Developer docs context.

sources.title: Write for a global audience (Google developer documentation style guide)
findings: Docs are written in US English with translation in mind.
Short unambiguous sentences, active voice, present tense, avoid colloquialisms, idioms, humor, seasonal references; keep terminology consistent.
sources.limits: Developer docs.

sources.title: Cross-references and linking (Google developer documentation style guide)
findings: Link text should make sense without surrounding text; do not use "click here" or "this document".
sources.limits: none

sources.title: Microsoft Writing Style Guide - brand voice (simple and human) and welcome
findings: Guide's voice principle is "above all, simple and human" (page title); detailed rules not extracted this session.
sources.limits: Only the voice and welcome pages were fetched (welcome: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/welcome/); thin evidence.
sources.revisit: extract bias-free communication and procedures pages

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide - Voice and Tone
findings: Voice stays constant, tone adapts to the situation.
Use active voice, avoid slang and jargon, write positively.
sources.limits: Company brand guide, not evidence of effect.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
findings: Level A: users understand what each link does; provide descriptive link names or context.
Techniques accept link text alone or link text plus sentence or programmatic context.
sources.limits: Context-dependent: link text alone is not always required for conformance.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
findings: Level AA: headings and labels describe topic or purpose; helps orientation.
sources.limits: Does not require headings to exist or to be unique.

sources.title: git SubmittingPatches
findings: Describe changes in imperative mood, as if giving orders to the codebase.
Make the explanation understandable without external resources; summarize linked discussions instead of only linking.
sources.limits: Git project's own mailing-list workflow; git-commit man page (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit) opened but no subject-length rule extracted.

sources.title: Creating a pull request template for your repository (GitHub Docs)
findings: A PR template's contents appear automatically in the pull request body.
sources.limits: Location rules not extracted.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System - Content foundations
findings: Content foundations aim for clear, concise, consistent language in Atlassian apps.
sources.limits: Product UI copy guidance, not Confluence documentation guidance. No official Atlassian doc-writing guide found; community posts seen in search were not opened.
sources.revisit: look for Atlassian Team Playbook or Confluence docs guidance

sources.title: Shape Up chapter 13 Show Progress (hill charts)
findings: Hill chart: uphill = figuring things out, downhill = making it happen.
First third uphill = "I've thought about this", second = "approach validated", final = "no other unknowns believed".
Backsliding happens when uphill work was done "with the head instead of the hands".
sources.limits: Method from one company; no outcome data.

sources.title: Lesbarkeitsindex (German Wikipedia)
findings: Amstad adapted Flesch for German: FRE_de = 180 - ASL - 58.5 x ASW (ASL average sentence length, ASW average syllables per word).
Word length dominates in both Flesch indices, which limits applicability to German with many compounds.
Formulas measure two surface features directly and others only indirectly.
sources.limits: Encyclopedia, secondary; LIX article not separately opened.
sources.revisit: replace with Amstad 1978 and Bjornsson (LIX) primary sources

sources.title: Bottom line up front (Wikipedia)
findings: BLUF originates in US Army Regulation 25-50: main point first and active voice.
Resembles the journalistic inverted pyramid; deductive rather than inductive order.
sources.limits: Secondary; the AR itself and Minto's book not opened. Pyramid Principle primary not reached.

sources.title: Mayer's 12 Principles of Multimedia Learning (summary)
findings: Signaling: cues emphasizing key information and structure help learning (outline slide, arrows, bold).
Redundancy: graphics with narration beat graphics plus narration plus on-screen text.
Coherence: remove irrelevant material.
sources.limits: Practitioner summary of lab-based learning research, not a meta-analysis; about learning lessons, not marketing persuasion or hero animation. Signaling meta-analysis page (rex.libraries.wsu.edu) opened but only a title, no content.
sources.revisit: read Mayer 2009/2014 and the 2020 signaling meta-analysis in ETR&D 68(5)

sources.title: Duden Rechtschreibregeln
findings: Free reference of spelling and punctuation rules by number (e.g. D 100 to D 108 for comma in enumerations; D 5 to D 11 for quotation marks).
sources.limits: Rules index, not style advice; does not confirm the 2024 Regelwerk date.
sources.revisit: pair with Rat primary when reachable

sources.title: FaST Guide, Version 3.0
findings: Expands FaST as Fluid Scaling Technology.
The group of people working together is the Collective; everyone in it is a Member; a Collective can work on several products with several Product Managers.
Teams self-organize around work items in a Marketplace and record choices on a Marketplace Board; Discovery Trees break down work and track progress.
sources.limits: Read from a local PDF copy of v3.0 (January 2024); the web URL was not opened in this session. Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: cite, do not adapt.

sources.title: ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language - Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines
findings: Plain language standard: readers find what they need, understand it, and use it; principles are relevance, findability, clarity (sentences, paragraphs, structure), and succinctness.
sources.limits: Cited by standard number. The iso.org page returned 403 on 2026-11-24 and the URL was not opened; the standard text was not seen. It sets principles and asks to test with readers; the numeric targets in the reference-page profile are local working values, not values from the standard.
sources.revisit: open the ISO 24495-1:2023 abstract when iso.org is reachable and confirm the URL

sources.title: DIN 8581-1:2024-05 Einfache Sprache - Anwendung für das Deutsche - Teil 1: Sprachspezifische Festlegungen
findings: German plain-language standard (Einfache Sprache) for factual texts; builds on DIN ISO 24495-1, makes its recommendations specific to German and raises some to requirements.
Its target audience does not explicitly include readers with cognitive impairments; Leichte Sprache is not part of it.
sources.limits: Only the DIN Media catalog page was opened (2026-11-24); the standard text itself is paid and was not seen, so no rule inside it is quoted.
sources.revisit: yearly; check for a newer edition or Part 2

sources.title: ISO 24495-2:2025 Plain language - Part 2: Legal communication
findings: First edition (August 2025) of plain-language guidance for legal communication; builds on ISO 24495-1.
sources.limits: Known from search-result snippets of iso.org and resellers; the iso.org page and the standard text were not opened.
sources.revisit: open the iso.org page when reachable

sources.title: Rat für deutsche Rechtschreibung: Geschlechtergerechte Schreibung, Pressemitteilung vom 15.12.2023
findings: Word-internal gender characters (star, colon, underscore) are not admitted into the core orthography (Kernbestand); the Council handles them in a separate supplement on Sonderzeichen and keeps observing usage.
Whether such forms count as errors in schools and administration is for the responsible state bodies, and some bodies prohibit them.
sources.limits: Seen only through search-result summaries; the PDF itself was not opened, so wording and the decision date are second-hand. Press reports are consistent.
sources.revisit: open the Rat's supplement on Sonderzeichen and check for a newer decision

sources.title: Rat für deutsche Rechtschreibung: revised Amtliches Regelwerk binding since 1 July 2024
findings: The revised Amtliches Regelwerk with the new word list has been binding for schools and administration since 1 July 2024; implementation runs through transition periods coordinated by the state bodies.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 and read through a summarizing fetch tool. Binding for schools and administration, not for private writers. No source found for a July 2025 date.

sources.title: GOV.UK Writing to GOV.UK standards: Clear language
findings: "Try to split up sentences that are over 25 words long."
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24. A prompt to check and split, not a hard rule; the older A to Z URL returned 404 and the sentence was not found in the A to Z page.

sources.title: Schriver, K. A. (2017). Plain Language in the US Gains Momentum: 1940-2015. IEEE Transactions on Professional Communication 60(4), 343-383
findings: Review of US plain-language practice: readability formulas are often unreliable and invalid for judging text quality; reader-focused testing is the standard for knowing what is plain (as summarized by the Center for Plain Language).
sources.limits: Read as a summary from the Center for Plain Language and a pre-publication draft listing; the published paper was not opened.
sources.revisit: open the published paper and the Center summary

sources.title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing
findings: Descriptive list of signs, not proof; indicators change across model generations and some older ones are much rarer in newer models.
Lists em-dash overuse (2022 to September 2026) under historical indicators, most useful in combination with other indicators; some newer models avoid em dashes.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 (page text partly read through a summarizing fetch tool); no revision date is shown, the page says "As of October 2026". A living page: re-read before an audit.

sources.title: van der Bles, van der Linden, Freeman, Spiegelhalter (2020). The effects of communicating uncertainty on public trust in facts and numbers. PNAS 117(14), 7672-7683
findings: Five experiments (n = 5,780, including a BBC News field experiment): people perceive more uncertainty when it is communicated, but trust in the numbers and the source falls only a little, and mostly for verbal uncertainty communication.
sources.limits: Abstract opened via PubMed Central on 2026-11-24; the body was not read. Study populations are UK and US adults; effects are small, so the rule is a preference, not a guarantee.

sources.title: Diataxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation
findings: Four documentation types for four user needs: tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanation.
Crossing or blurring the boundaries between them is named as the root of many documentation problems.
sources.limits: Home and start-here pages opened on 2026-11-24; the page states no explicit one-type-per-page rule, so that rule is this catalog's inference from the boundary guidance.

sources.title: MADR 4.0.0 Markdown Architectural Decision Records
findings: MADR 4.0.0 (2024-09-17) template sections: title, context and problem statement, decision drivers (optional), considered options, decision outcome with consequences and confirmation (optional), pros and cons of the options (optional), more information (optional).
sources.limits: Project page opened on 2026-11-24; the template file was not read.

sources.title: Wikipedia (de): Anzeichen für KI-generierte Inhalte (WP:AKI)
findings: Lists German indicators: chat residue ("Ich hoffe, das hilft", "Natürlich!", letter-style greetings, knowledge-cutoff phrases, placeholders), stiff "nicht nur ..., sondern auch" parallels and participle clauses carried over from English, vague authorities ("Branchenberichte", "Einige Kritiker"), stock verb phrases ("steht als", "dient als Zeugnis"), bold emphasis, emoji before headings, Markdown residue.
The page says no indicator is conclusive alone; only fabricated sources or chat residue justify quick deletion.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 through a summarizing fetch tool; wording of section names not checked verbatim. A living page: re-read before an audit.

sources.title: Prompting best practices (Claude developer documentation)
findings: Context or motivation behind an instruction helps Claude deliver more targeted responses.
Tell Claude what to do instead of what not to do.
Newer models are more responsive to the system prompt; emphasis such as "CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool when..." can now overtrigger, so use plain wording such as "Use this tool when...".
For the newest models, blanket instructions to verify at the end or to use a subagent to verify cause over-verification; constrain the scope and say when to delegate.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 (full text saved and searched for the quoted lines). Vendor guidance for Claude models; it changes with each model generation. The over-verification finding comes from a research pass on 2026-11-24 and was not re-quoted.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
findings: Aim for the smallest possible set of high-signal tokens; minimal does not have to mean short.
Hardcoded rule-heavy prompts are brittle and vague guidance gives no signal; aim between them.
Curate diverse, canonical examples instead of a laundry list of edge cases.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 through a summarizing fetch tool; publication date not confirmed beyond the year. Vendor engineering guidance, not a controlled study.

sources.title: Gloaguen et al. (2026). Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents? arXiv:2602.11988
findings: Context files do not generally improve task success and raise inference cost by over 20 percent on average.
The result held for LLM-generated and developer-committed files; developer-written files gained 2.4 percent, not significant; agents follow the instructions, but repository overviews did not help.
Context files are useful for non-standard practices; evaluate any change before deployment.
sources.limits: Abstract and v3 (revised 2026-09-29) opened on 2026-11-24; the +2.4 percent figure and its non-significance come from a research pass on the same day. Coding-agent benchmark with several coding agents, not a writing study.

sources.title: GPT-5 prompting guide (OpenAI Cookbook)
findings: Contradictory instructions cost reasoning effort because the model tries to reconcile them; removing contradictions and ambiguities improved results.
An emphatic "Be THOROUGH" prompt that worked on older models made GPT-5 over-use tools until the emphasis was softened.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 through a summarizing fetch tool; the page is marked archived and may reference outdated models.

sources.title: Niederhoffer et al. (2025). AI-Generated "Workslop" Is Destroying Productivity. Harvard Business Review
sources.publisher: Harvard Business Review (BetterUp Labs, Stanford Social Media Lab)
findings: Names "workslop": AI-generated work that looks polished but lacks substance and shifts the work to the receiver; based on a survey of US workers.
sources.limits: Only the title, authors and date were confirmed on 2026-11-24; the page excerpt cut off before the survey results, so figures are not cited. Survey, not an experiment.

sources.title: DIN SPEC 33429:2025-03 Empfehlungen für Deutsche Leichte Sprache
findings: Current DIN SPEC (60 pages) with recommendations for writing, translating and designing texts in German Easy Language (Leichte Sprache), including language rules and the qualifications of writers and reviewers; replaces the 2023-04 draft.
sources.limits: Metadata confirmed through a web search on 2026-11-24; the document text was not opened.

sources.title: DIN ISO 24495-2:2025-12 Einfache Sprache - Teil 2: Juristische Kommunikation
findings: German edition of ISO 24495-2:2025 (legal communication), builds on part 1, with checklist annex and German examples.
sources.limits: Metadata and table of contents confirmed through a web search on 2026-11-24; the text was not opened.

sources.title: Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG)
findings: German law implementing Directive (EU) 2019/882 on accessibility requirements for products and services; § 7 sets information duties of the manufacturer.
sources.limits: The page was opened on 2026-11-24 but lists only headings; the application date 2025-06-28 and the wording of the understandability duty were not confirmed from it. Whether a given product is in scope needs legal review.

sources.title: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha (2025). AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances. CHI 2025, arXiv:2409.11360
findings: Controlled experiment with 118 participants from India and the US: suggestions from a Western-centric writing assistant moved Indian participants toward Western writing styles and cut their cultural nuance.
sources.limits: Abstract opened on 2026-11-24. It studies style homogenization from AI suggestions, not translation: it does not test English drafts translated into German.

sources.title: Rogers and Lasky-Fink: Write shorter messages (HKS Behavioral Insights; book "Writing for Busy Readers", 2023)
findings: Field experiment with 7,002 school leaders: a 49-word request email drew a 4.8 percent response and a 127-word version 2.7 percent; readers of the short email were more likely to expect a quick task.
sources.limits: The figures come from web search summaries of the authors' material on 2026-11-24; the HKS PDF itself was not opened. One population and one request type; the effect of length alone is not separated from the effect of the request count.

sources.title: Ahrefs: We Analyzed 137K Sites: 97% of llms.txt Files Never Get Read
findings: Server logs of 137,210 domains: 97 percent of llms.txt files received no requests in May 2026; AI retrieval bots made about 1 percent of the requests that did arrive, and most requesting bots were not AI tools.
sources.limits: Figures from a web search summary on 2026-11-24; the article was not opened. It measures requests for the index file, not whether a bot used the content. The sample skews toward technical sites.

sources.title: John Mueller (Google), post on llms.txt, reported by PPC Land
findings: Google's John Mueller said no AI system currently uses llms.txt (as reported).
sources.limits: Second-hand: the original post was not found or opened on 2026-11-24. A vendor statement about the state of the art in mid-2025; it can change.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code documentation)
findings: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.
If two instructions contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily.
CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration; an instruction that must run at a fixed point belongs in a hook.
Block-level HTML comments in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected.
sources.limits: Opened on 2026-11-24 and searched for the quoted lines. Host documentation for Claude Code; other hosts differ.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md (Codex documentation)
findings: Codex concatenates AGENTS.md files from the project root to the working directory and stops adding files once the combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default.
sources.limits: Taken from a research pass on 2026-11-24; the default can be changed in Codex configuration.

sources.title: Jaroslawicz et al. (2025). How Many Instructions Can LLMs Follow at Once? (IFScale) arXiv:2507.11538
findings: Instruction-following accuracy falls as the number of simultaneous instructions grows.
Earlier instructions are followed more reliably than later ones.
sources.limits: Taken from a research pass on 2026-11-24; benchmark of keyword-inclusion instructions in a report task, not of agent context files.
